author: philly leader
title: Phillies consider Justin Crawford for major league outfield spot amid possible roster changes
text:
The Philadelphia Phillies are considering changes to their outfield for the 2026 season, with Justin Crawford emerging as a potential candidate for a roster spot during Spring Training. Crawford, who is ranked as the club’s No. 3 prospect and holds the No. 54 position on MLB’s overall prospect list, is seen as close to being ready for Major League play.
Team president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski addressed Crawford’s chances in October. “We have some young players that we’re going to mesh into our club,” Dombrowski told MLB.com’s Todd Zolecki. “I’m not going to declare that anybody has a job, but there will be some people that we’re really open minded to be on the big league club next year coming out of Spring Training … [Crawford] needs to go to camp and just do what he’s basically been doing.”
Crawford was selected by the Phillies in the first round (17th overall) of the 2022 draft from Las Vegas high school ranks. He has demonstrated strong plate discipline and notable speed throughout his minor league career, posting a .322 batting average and .385 on-base percentage while maintaining an 18.4 percent strikeout rate. In Triple-A this past season, Crawford recorded a .334 average, stole 46 bases, and achieved an .863 OPS.
His standout attribute is his speed—graded at 75—which influences both his offensive approach and base running ability. Over three full professional seasons, he has stolen at least 40 bases each year with an 82 percent success rate.
Offensively, Crawford consistently makes contact and gets on base frequently. Recent adjustments have increased his power output slightly; over two seasons he accumulated 48 doubles, eight triples, and 16 home runs.
Despite these strengths, there are concerns about his long-term power potential due to his swing profile which favors ground balls over fly balls. There is also debate about whether left field or center field would be his best defensive position; most evaluators see left field as optimal even though it traditionally requires more power production.
A comparison often made is with Carl Crawford—Justin’s father—a four-time All-Star who excelled in left field during his own career through speed rather than power.
Dombrowski indicated that team decisions regarding free agents could affect where Crawford fits into the lineup: if right fielder Nick Castellanos departs as expected and if slugger Kyle Schwarber re-signs or leaves via free agency will influence whether additional moves are made or if Crawford steps directly into a starting role.
